sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers the northwest side of central Ridgewood around the Erie Railroad station, with north toward the upper left. Its upper half lies between Madison Place, Heights Road, Corsa Terrace and West Ridgewood Avenue (labelled with the earlier name West Franklin Avenue in brackets east of Corsa Terrace), and holds a few large detached dwellings on deep lots. Further east, between Corsa Terrace and the Boulevard, stands the Geo. L. Pease Memorial Library, of brick with steam heat, and at the corner of West Ridgewood Avenue a cinder-block apartment building with brick and tile stores. The Boulevard curves around to the railroad, where the Erie Railroad main line runs down the east edge of the sheet past the passenger station and baggage room, with a tunnel and incline under the tracks. South of West Ridgewood Avenue the sheet shows the First Church of Christ, Scientist with its reading room, houses along Sherman Place and Washington Place, and on Godwin Avenue a solid row of concrete-block and brick stores. At Wilsey Square stand The Play House motion picture theatre with stage and scenery, a cement-block building with photo studio, a 30-car public garage, a block of stores with a bakery's portable ovens, a row of private garages, and buildings for a plumber. Water pipes up to 12 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: West Ridgewood Avenue is labelled with the earlier name West Franklin Avenue in brackets.
The Boulevard curving to the station is not a named street in OpenStreetMap; the station plaza is Garber Square and Wilsey Square today.
OpenStreetMap has two Heights Road / Madison Place nodes about 60 m apart; the eastern one (40.98241, -74.12352) matches the drawn junction.
Geo. L. Pease Memorial Library; First Church of Christ, Scientist; The Play House (motion pictures); public garage for 30 cars.
Erie Railroad main line with passenger station, baggage room and a pedestrian tunnel along the east edge.

Map, 50 ft. Single part. Madison Pl, Heights Rd, Corsa Ter, Boulevard, W. Ridgewood Av (W. Franklin Av), Sherman Pl, Washington Pl, Godwin Av, Wilsey Square; Erie station, Pease Memorial Library, Play House theatre. Rotation about -26 deg, unlike the 100 ft sheets (-12 to -19).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and covers the business centre of Ridgewood east of the Erie Railroad, with north toward the upper left. It runs from (W.) Franklin Avenue at the top to Passaic Street at the bottom, and from the Erie Railroad main line, with its tunnel, stairs, waiting room and the incline from the tunnel along Wilsey Square, east to (N.) Oak Street and Van Neste Square. North Broad and South Broad Streets run down the west side beside the tracks; Chestnut Street, a proposed street and Prospect Street cross the blocks, and Hudson and Dayton Streets meet Prospect Street in the south. The blocks along East (West) Ridgewood Avenue are solidly commercial: stores of brick, tile and concrete block, the First National Bank and Trust Co. of Ridgewood (fireproof, built 1930, drawn in brown), the Citizens National Bank and Trust Co., the Hopper, Hutton, Wilsey and Prospect buildings, Prospect Hall, drug stores and a candy factory. Other notable buildings are the Post Office, the Ridgewood News and Ridgewood Herald printing works, Hoffman's Storage Warehouse, a hall over stores, garages for 20, 30 and 50 cars, auto sales and repair shops and gasoline stations, the Fire Department headquarters (Engine Co. No. 1) with bell tower and siren, the Municipal Building with police headquarters, a city garage, the Ridgewood Opera House (not in use), and the Church of Our Lady of Mt. Carmel (R.C.) with its rectory. The I. E. Hutton Lumber & Supply Co. yard with lumber sheds and a siding lies between the tracks and South Broad Street. Dwellings and tenements fill the blocks east of Chestnut Street.
notes: Ridgewood Avenue is labelled "E. (W.) Ridgewood Av." east of the railroad and "W. Ridgewood Av." west of it; Franklin Avenue is labelled "(W.) Franklin Av." and Oak Street "(N.) Oak".
A 'Proposed Street' is drawn as a dashed line through the block between North Broad Street and Chestnut Street.
The First National Bank and Trust Co. of Ridgewood building is marked fireproof construction, built 1930.
The Fire Department headquarters note says 'for report see sheet No. 1'.
Ridgewood Opera House is marked 'not in use'.
Prospect, Hudson, Dayton and Passaic are Prospect Street, Hudson Street, Dayton Street and Passaic Street in OpenStreetMap.

Map, 50 ft. Single part. Business centre: (W.) Franklin Av, N. and S. Broad, Chestnut, (N.) Oak, E. (W.) Ridgewood Av, Van Neste Sq, Prospect, Hudson, Dayton, Passaic; Erie main line, Post Office, banks, Fire Dept, Municipal Bldg, Opera House, Mt. Carmel R.C. church, Hutton lumber yard.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the Upper Ridgewood district of northern Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet is bounded roughly by Avondale Road at the top, Phelps Road at the bottom, Morningside Road on the left and Upper Boulevard and Hillcrest Road across the upper right. Heights Road runs the length of the sheet, with a short jog near California, crossing Glenwood, Sherwood, California, Fairmount and Phelps Roads. Almost all of the ground is built with detached frame dwellings of one and two storeys, each with a small frame garage, and a few veneered brick houses, several marked 'From Plans'. The largest building is the Willard School on Morningside Road at California, a brick school with gymnasium, stage and auditorium, heated by steam and lit by electricity. St. Elizabeth Church (Episcopal) and its parish house stand between Fairmount and California, and the Upper Ridgewood Community Church stands near Sherwood Road at the right edge. The right side of the sheet is cut by the diagonal of Upper Boulevard and Hillcrest Road, which meet Glenwood Road near a compass rose and the printed sheet label. Six-inch water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and telephone hydrant boxes are marked along most streets. Block numbers 605 to 608 and 6 to 24 are printed, and the margins refer to adjoining sheets 7, 10 and 18.
notes: Heights Road is labelled with Argyle Road in brackets along its upper block; OpenStreetMap carries both as Heights Road.
Morningside Road is labelled with Boulevard in brackets; modern name Morningside Road.
Barrington Road (Madison) and Phelps Road (Jefferson) show older names in brackets; modern names Barrington Road and Phelps Road.
California is lettered without a suffix; it is California Street in OpenStreetMap.
Virginia Place and Summit Avenue are not in the street extract by those names.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Upper Ridgewood: Avondale, Glenwood, Sherwood, Fairmount, Phelps (Jefferson) Roads; Heights Rd (Argyle Rd), California, Morningside Rd (Boulevard), Upper Boulevard, Barrington Rd (Madison); Willard School.

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of sheet 9 covers the residential area of northern Ridgewood between East Glen Avenue (labelled 'E. Glen Av. (Harrison Av.)') and Meadowbrook Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. A heavy line across the lower third of the sheet separates it from a second part drawn further east. On the west the abandoned right of way of the North Side Rapid Transit Co. (Electric) runs down the sheet beside Northern Parkway (Lexington Avenue); Van Buren (Madison Avenue) and Sterling Place enter from the north, where the blocks belong to sheet 8. South of East Glen Avenue, Down (Park Avenue) crosses the sheet, and Libby, Pearsall, Fairfield and Bogert Avenues run down to Meadowbrook Avenue. Much of the ground is still open: large lots along Northern Parkway, a vacant block east of Fairfield Avenue and open tracts north of East Glen Avenue. The one large building is the Harrison Avenue School, a brick building with steam heat and electric light, standing in an open block between Fairfield and Bogert Avenues. Elsewhere the sheet shows one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages, a few veneered brick houses, a waiting room on the trolley right of way, and water pipes of 6 inches with hydrants and fire alarm boxes.
notes: East Glen Avenue is labelled with its earlier name, Harrison Avenue, in brackets.
Van Buren is labelled with the earlier name Madison Avenue in brackets; the junction with East Glen Avenue matches modern Van Buren Street.
Northern Parkway is labelled with the earlier name Lexington Avenue in brackets.
Down (Park Avenue) has no counterpart in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used for control.
North Side Rapid Transit Co. (Electric) right of way, marked abandoned, with a waiting room at East Glen Avenue.
Harrison Avenue School between Fairfield and Bogert Avenues.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line. Part 1 (main, top): E. Glen Av (Harrison Av) to Meadowbrook Av; Van Buren (Madison Av), Northern Parkway (Lexington Av), Sterling Pl, Down (Park Av), Libby, Pearsall, Fairfield, Bogert; Harrison Av School. Part 2 (lower): Valleau Cemetery, E. Glen Av from Valleau Av to Franklin Turnpike, Westfield, N. Pleasant, Corona Pl, Walthery, Hickory, Concord Rd (Brookline Av), Eastern Parkway; Paramus Dutch Reformed Church, Saddle River.

sheet-9-2.description: The lower part of sheet 9, below a heavy dividing line, shows a separate area east of the main part: East Glen Avenue (labelled 'E. Glen Av. (Harrison Av.)') from Valleau Avenue east to Franklin Turnpike and the Saddle River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing toward the upper left. North of East Glen Avenue lies the open ground of Valleau Cemetery, with no graves or buildings drawn, and on the east Franklin Turnpike and West Saddle River Road leave the sheet toward the north. South of East Glen Avenue a small grid of house lots runs along Westfield Avenue (marked 'Not Opened'), North Pleasant Avenue, Corona Place and Walthery Avenue to Hickory and Concord Road (Brookline Avenue), with Eastern Parkway curving through the open blocks B3 and B4. Most lots hold one- or two-storey frame dwellings and garages, some marked 'From Plans 1930'. At the junction of East Glen Avenue and Franklin Turnpike stands the Paramus Dutch Reformed Church, with a spire, steam heat and electric light, its Sunday school and two long horse sheds, and a store on Walthery Avenue. Franklin Turnpike crosses the Saddle River by a concrete bridge in the southeast corner; an older loop of the turnpike curves into East Glen Avenue west of the church.
notes: Separate area drawn below a heavy line on sheet 9, east of the main part.
Concord Road is labelled with the earlier name Brookline Avenue in brackets; Hickory is Hickory Street in OpenStreetMap.
Westfield Avenue is marked 'Not Opened' south of East Glen Avenue.
Paramus Dutch Reformed Church with Sunday school and horse sheds at East Glen Avenue and Franklin Turnpike.
Franklin Turnpike near the church has been realigned since; its junctions were not used for control.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts separated by a heavy line. Part 1 (main, top): E. Glen Av (Harrison Av) to Meadowbrook Av; Van Buren (Madison Av), Northern Parkway (Lexington Av), Sterling Pl, Down (Park Av), Libby, Pearsall, Fairfield, Bogert; Harrison Av School. Part 2 (lower): Valleau Cemetery, E. Glen Av from Valleau Av to Franklin Turnpike, Westfield, N. Pleasant, Corona Pl, Walthery, Hickory, Concord Rd (Brookline Av), Eastern Parkway; Paramus Dutch Reformed Church, Saddle River.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the western part of Upper Ridgewood south of Phelps Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Phelps Road crosses the top of the sheet, Morningside Road and Monroe Street converge at the upper left, and West Glen Avenue runs across the middle. Monroe Street cuts diagonally from the upper left to the foot of the sheet at Valleyview Avenue. The right half is a regular suburban grid of Alpine Terrace, Wastena Terrace, Kemah Road, Waiku Road, Te-Ke-Nink Road and Udahli Avenue, with curving streets around Unadilla Road in the lower right; nearly every lot carries a detached one- or two-storey frame dwelling and garage, many marked 'From Plans'. The left half is largely undeveloped: long subdivided lots in blocks 614 and 615 laid out along Patston and an unnamed street marked 'Not Named' and 'Not Opened', with Waiku Road and Beechwood Road only partly built. A strip along the left edge is lettered 'See Map of Midland Park' and marks the village limits of Midland Park and Ridgewood, with Franklin Turnpike and Midland Park labelled where the turnpike crosses the corner. Six- and eight-inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the built-up streets. A compass rose and a 100 foot scale bar are printed at the bottom left. Block numbers run from 6 to 21 at the upper side and 45 to 55 below, with 612 to 615 on the western blocks.
notes: Wastena Terrace is also spelled 'Westena' in brackets on the sheet; OpenStreetMap carries Wastena Terrace.
Te-Ke-Nink Road is Carlton Terrace in OpenStreetMap and Udahli Avenue is Windsor Terrace.
Monroe Street is North Monroe Street and Valleyview Avenue is Valley View Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Alpine Terrace carries Oak Knoll Road in brackets on the curved top block; Heights Road in brackets on South Hill Road.
The left margin reads 'See Map of Midland Park'; the strip beyond the village limits is blank.
Waiku Road is printed so on the sheet; the index spells it Waikee Road.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Phelps Rd to Valleyview Av; Monroe St, W. Glen Av, Alpine and Wastena Terraces, Te-Ke-Nink Rd (now Carlton Terrace), Udahli Av (now Windsor Terrace), Waiku Rd, Kemah Rd, Patston (arbitrary); Midland Park limits on the left.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows a residential district of Upper Ridgewood south of Valleyview Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Monroe Street runs down the middle of the sheet and Heights Road along the right edge. East of Monroe Street the blocks between Woodland Avenue, Sheridan Terrace, Monte Vista Avenue and Madison Place, and the blocks along Park Slope, are built up with detached frame dwellings of one and two storeys with garages, some veneered or tile, and one building marked as a private school, heated by steam and lit by electricity, on Heights Road near Monte Vista Avenue. Unadilla Road makes a loop at the top. West of Monroe Street the ground is much more open: Beechwood Road is built only on its east side, and a large tract in blocks 64 and 615 is nearly vacant, crossed by Patston Street, marked as arbitrary, which curves down toward Murray Avenue. A few houses and a water tower stand along Clinton Avenue and Murray Avenue at the lower left, where long narrow lots in blocks 66 and 67 run down to West Ridgewood Avenue. Hillside Place curves from Monte Vista Avenue down to West Ridgewood Avenue. One house near the lower right is marked 'Damaged by Fire'. Six- and eight-inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, and the scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: West Ridgewood Avenue is labelled with West Franklin Avenue in brackets, an older name.
Sheridan Terrace is labelled with Heights Terrace in brackets; OpenStreetMap carries Sheridan Terrace.
Monroe is North Monroe Street and Valleyview is Valley View Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Hillside Place is North Hillside Place.
Murray Avenue and Patston Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract by those names.
The Heights Road / Monte Vista Avenue junction was rejected as 17 m from the fit.
Map, 100 ft. Single part. Monroe, Woodland, Sheridan Ter (Heights Ter), Monte Vista, Madison Pl, Park Slope, Hillside Pl, Murray Av, W. Ridgewood Av (W. Franklin Av).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the eastern side of Upper Ridgewood where the residential streets meet the railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. On the left, detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages line Valleyview Avenue, Woodland Avenue, Sunset Avenue, Monte Vista Avenue, Ridge Road, Madison Place and Heights Road, in blocks 62, 63, 71, 72, 75 and 76. Crest Road sweeps through the middle of the sheet in a long curve, labelled Hillcrest Drive in the upper part and Overlook Avenue near Ridge Road, and beyond it blocks 60, 72 and 77 are largely vacant. The Erie Railroad main line, a broad multiple-track strip marked 'Railroad Pl.' and 'Arbitrary', crosses the sheet from top to bottom. East of the tracks, near the bottom, is a small industrial and commercial area along Commerce Place and West Franklin Avenue: a lumber yard with scattered lumber storage, the Young and Bortic coal, wood and feed yard with its chutes and sheds, a Public Service Corporation of New Jersey electric sub-station, a bowling alley, a garage and auto repair shops, a printing shop, a plumber and the Y.M.C.A. Further north on the east side, Douglas Place, Chestnut Street and Robinson Lane bound blocks 171 and 190, where dwellings face Oak Street along the right edge. The upper right is blank apart from Mastin Place. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed on the sheet.
notes: Mastin Place is labelled with Hillside Avenue in brackets; Crest Road carries Hillcrest Drive and Overlook Avenue in brackets.
Oak and Franklin are printed with bracketed N. and W.; OpenStreetMap carries Oak Street and Franklin Avenue.
Boulevard on this sheet is marked 'Not Opened'.
Robinson Lane was left out of the georeferencing: its junctions sat 5 m off the fit to the other streets.
Railroad Place and Commerce Place along the Erie Railroad are marked arbitrary.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Crest Rd, Heights Rd, Sunset, Monte Vista, Ridge Rd, Madison Pl; Erie main line with Railroad Pl and Commerce Pl (arbitrary), lumber and coal yards (Young & Bortic), Public Service sub-station, Y.M.C.A.; Douglas Pl, Robinson Lane, Chestnut, (N.) Oak, (W.) Franklin Av. Robinson Lane left out here (junctions about 5 m off).

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the northern edge of the central village of Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Mastin Place bounds the top and West Franklin Avenue the bottom of the western blocks, with Oak and Walnut Streets on the left and North Maple Avenue running diagonally from the top to the lower right. Linwood Avenue and Robinson Lane cross the sheet from left to right. The western blocks (619, 173, 174, 175, 191, 192 and 193) are a close pattern of detached frame dwellings of one and two storeys with garages, with a few tile or brick houses. Cottage Place curves between North Walnut Street and North Maple Avenue. Institutions near the bottom include the Unitarian Church on Cottage Place, Christ Church, Ridgewood Secretarial School and the fireproof Franklin-Maples Apartments, built 1927, along West Franklin Avenue. The B.P.O.E. Club House stands in open ground east of North Maple Avenue. The upper right is mostly vacant land in blocks 176 and 177, crossed by Hohokus Brook, which loops down toward the right edge and is crossed by East Linwood Avenue. The abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit Company electric right of way runs down the right edge. In the lower right corner, Marshall Avenue and East Franklin Avenue serve a small group of houses on narrow lots in block 200. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Mastin Place is labelled with Hillside Avenue in brackets.
Oak and Walnut are printed with bracketed N.; OpenStreetMap carries Oak Street and North Walnut Street.
Linwood Avenue is lettered with W. and E. in brackets; OpenStreetMap carries Linwood Avenue.
Marshall Avenue and Beech Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract by those names.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (Electric) right of way is marked abandoned.
Map, 100 ft. Single part. Mastin Pl (Hillside Av), Douglas Pl, Linwood Av, Robinson Lane, N. Oak, N. Walnut, Cottage Pl, N. Maple Av, Franklin Av, Marshall Av; Hohokus Brook.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a residential district of northeastern Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Meadowbrook Avenue at the top to Beverly Road at the bottom, and from the abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit right of way and Hohokus Brook on the west to North Van Dien Avenue on the east edge. Between Meadowbrook Avenue and Linwood Avenue, north-south streets (Libby, Pearsall, Fairfield and Bogert Avenues) end at a strip of land shown as two parallel unopened streets, one marked 'Not Opened' and one 'Not Named', so the middle of the upper half is largely vacant ground. South of Linwood Avenue the blocks are regularly subdivided along Fairway Road, Colonial Road, Overbrook Road and Beverly Road, crossed by Collingwood Place and Hampton Place, with almost every lot holding a one- or two-storey frame dwelling and a frame or concrete-block auto garage. A few veneered brick dwellings, some marked 'From Plans', stand near Meadowbrook Avenue. In the southwest corner Hohokus Brook runs diagonally beside Park Way (an unopened road) and the abandoned electric railway right of way, past a few scattered houses on North Irving Street and the end of Marshall Avenue. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches, hydrants and a fire alarm box at Linwood Avenue are marked. There are no commercial or industrial buildings; the sheet records an inter-war suburb of detached houses being built out on a regular grid.
notes: Linwood Avenue is labelled "(E.) Linwood Av."; it is Linwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Two parallel strips between Meadowbrook and Linwood Avenues are marked 'Not Opened' and 'Not Named'.
Park Way along Hohokus Brook is marked 'Not Opened'.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (Elec.) right of way, marked abandoned, crosses the southwest corner.
Modern Bogert Avenue meets Fairfield Avenue; on the sheet Bogert Avenue ends at the unopened strip, and that junction was excluded.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Meadowbrook Av to Beverly Rd, Libby, Pearsall, Fairfield, Bogert, N. Van Dien Av, (E.) Linwood Av, Fairway Rd, Collingwood Pl, Hampton Pl, Colonial Rd, Overbrook Rd, N. Irving, Park Way (not opened); Hohokus Brook and abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit right of way. Pilot sheet.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers a residential district in the north-east of Ridgewood east of North Van Dien Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. East Linwood Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet and North Pleasant Avenue runs down its centre from Concord Road at the top to Wyndemere Avenue at the bottom. Between Shelton Road and Linwood Avenue the blocks along Steilen Avenue are built with narrow lots of detached frame dwellings, several of brick or tile, while west of Steilen Avenue a large tract in block 153 is open ground with only a few houses. South of Linwood Avenue the blocks between Fairway Road, John Street, Knickerbocker Road and Wyndemere Avenue (blocks 217 to 222) are filled with one- and two-storey dwellings and garages, some marked 'From Plans'. In the east, Emmett Place, Waltherly Avenue and Wall Street divide larger blocks (154, 224, 225, 226) that are still mostly vacant, with a loop of unopened streets on the right marked 'Not Opened' near block 626. Waltherly Avenue is marked as not opened in its upper part. A small cooperative store is marked in block B8. Water pipes of four to eight inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown along the main streets. A compass rose is printed at the upper left and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Concord Road is labelled with Brookline Avenue in brackets.
Fairway Road is labelled with Wentworth Place in brackets for its eastern block.
Linwood Avenue is lettered with E. in brackets; OpenStreetMap carries Linwood Avenue.
John is John Street, and Wall is Wall Street, in OpenStreetMap; Waltherly Avenue is not in the extract.
Linwood Avenue / Steilen Avenue and North Pleasant Avenue / Shelton Road were rejected as 11 m and 8 m from the fit.
Waltherly Avenue is printed so on this sheet; the index and sheet 9 spell it Walthery (Walthery Avenue in OpenStreetMap).

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Concord Rd (Brookline Av), Shelton Rd, Steilen Av, N. Van Dien, Linwood, N. Pleasant, Fairway, Wentworth Pl, John, Knickerbocker Rd, Wyndemere, Wall, Emmett Pl, Waltherly Av (not opened).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the western edge of Ridgewood against the Midland Park village line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north is toward the upper left at about 30 degrees. West Ridgewood Avenue crosses the top and Godwin Avenue the middle, while Cantrell Road runs along the bottom. Clinton Avenue, Murray Avenue, Highland Avenue, Claremont Road and West End Avenue run roughly north to south between them. The northern blocks, 78 to 80, are only partly built: narrow lots lie along Ridgewood Avenue and Clinton Avenue, a large property with a long frame dwelling stands in block 79, and Maynard Court curves off West Ridgewood Avenue past several brick and frame houses. Below Godwin Avenue the blocks 96 to 100 and 627 are closely built with detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, with larger houses near West End Avenue, Ferris Place and Melrose Place. A former Public Service Corporation trolley right of way, marked abandoned, crosses the sheet diagonally in the lower left and again below Murray Avenue. The village limit between Midland Park and Ridgewood is drawn as a dash-dot line along Ridgewood Avenue (Maltbie Avenue) and across the lower left, and the margin beyond it is lettered 'See Map of Midland Park'. A water tower stands at the right edge. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, with the scale bar and compass at the top and bottom.
notes: West Ridgewood Avenue is labelled with West Franklin Avenue in brackets, an older name.
Grant is labelled with Hillcrest Road in brackets; Grant Avenue and Hillside Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Murray Avenue is North Murray Avenue and South Murray Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The rotation of the sheet (about -30 degrees) is larger than the neighbouring sheets (-11 to -17 degrees).
Public Service Corporation trolley right of way is marked abandoned.

Map, 100 ft, drawn at about -30 deg. Single part. W. Ridgewood Av, Maltbie, Clinton, Murray, Maynard Ct, Hillside Pl, Godwin, Lake, Mountain, Grant (Hillcrest Rd), Highland, Claremont, West End, Ferris Pl, Carolina, Melrose, Cantrell; Midland Park limits on the left.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers a residential district in the south-west of Ridgewood below Cantrell Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left at about 35 degrees. Cantrell Road and Melrose Place bound the top, Mountain Avenue runs down the left edge and Lincoln Avenue down the right. Highland Avenue, Claremont Road and West End Avenue run diagonally through the middle, crossed by Bellair Avenue, Orchard Place and West End Avenue's loop toward Lincoln Avenue. The blocks (101 to 107, 119 to 129) are built mainly with detached frame dwellings of one and two storeys with garages, some of brick or tile, and several larger houses on generous lots in blocks 105, 121, 122 and 125. Grandview Avenue sweeps round a semicircle at the lower middle, where wedge-shaped lots radiate from a single point on the circle. McKinley Place runs along the foot of the sheet and again at the right edge, where a stretch is marked 'Not Opened'. The upper right, around block 101, and the lower right, around blocks 126 and 129, are mostly vacant ground. Six-inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets. A compass rose is printed at the top and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Bellair Avenue is Bellair Road in OpenStreetMap.
Grandview Avenue corresponds to Grandview Circle in OpenStreetMap.
A stretch of McKinley Place on the right edge is marked 'Not Opened'.
The rotation of the sheet (about -36 degrees) is larger than the northern sheets of the atlas (-11 to -17 degrees).
Map, 100 ft, drawn at about -36 deg. Single part. Cantrell, Melrose, Carolina, Bellair, West End, Orchard Pl, Claremont, Highland, Mountain, Lincoln, Grandview Av, McKinley Pl.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers a residential district in the west-central part of Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Madison Place and Heights Road at the top, past West Ridgewood Avenue (West Franklin Avenue) and Washington Place, to Godwin Avenue, Ackerman Avenue and Lenox Avenue at the bottom. A compass rose sits in the unbuilt upper left corner. The largest building is the George Washington School, elementary and junior high, a brick and steel structure standing in a block between Monroe, Washington Place, Garfield Place and Godwin Avenue. Fornachon Hall School stands in a large lot to the west, and The West Side Presbyterian Church lies on West Ridgewood Avenue, with the Woman's Club and its auditorium on the block above. Most other lots hold detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages; the blocks along Godwin Avenue, Melrose Place and Lincoln Place are densely built, while the western blocks (marked 16 and 80) are large lots with few buildings. A strip marked as an abandoned Public Service Corporation trolley right of way crosses the sheet from west to east just north of the school. Ackerman Avenue runs diagonally from Godwin Avenue to the lower right past Spencer Place and Lenox Avenue, with a dashed double line along it. A few blocks at the bottom are partly blank. Water pipes, hydrants, fire alarm boxes and house numbers are marked throughout. Block numbers 80 to 92, 101, 106 and 108 are printed, and neighbouring sheets 2, 11, 12, 16, 17 and 19 are named at the margins.
notes: West Ridgewood Avenue is labelled with the old name "(W. Franklin Av.)" in brackets; OpenStreetMap has West Ridgewood Avenue.
Monroe is South Monroe Street in OpenStreetMap; Hillside Place and Lincoln Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
A Public Service Corporation trolley right of way is marked abandoned.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. W. Ridgewood Av (W. Franklin Av), Madison Pl, Heights Rd, Hillside Pl, Monroe, Washington Pl, Garfield Pl, Sherman Pl, Godwin Av, Ethelbert, Doremus, Ackerman, Spencer Pl, Lenox, Melrose, Lincoln Pl; George Washington School, West Side Presbyterian Church.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the southern edge of Ridgewood's central district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The Erie Railroad main line, a broad band of parallel tracks marked 'Main Line', runs down the middle of the sheet. East of the tracks, South Broad Street (also lettered as Zabriskie Av.) runs south from Passaic Street past the I. E. Hutton lumber yard with its sheds, Our Lady of Mount Carmel School and an auditorium marked 'From Plans', and an auto sales and service building at Essex Street. Le Roy Place, Brainard Place and Woodside Avenue open into blocks of detached dwellings; farther south, Leonard Place, Boyce Place, Highwood Avenue and Edwards Street run diagonally to the southeast, with a church near Highwood Avenue. At the lower right the Ridgewood and Glen Rock village limits cross High Street, and the area beyond is marked 'See Map of Glen Rock' and left blank. West of the tracks the sheet shows a regular grid of small residential blocks between Doremus Avenue and the railroad: Ethelbert, Lenox, Richmond and Christopher Avenues and Randolph Place, with Evangelical Lutheran Bethlehem church at Lenox Avenue. Pomander Walk, a short street of brick row-type dwellings ending in a circular turning space, lies near the top, near The Amethyst Hotel. At the lower left stand the Public Service Corporation of N.J. gas plant with its gas holder on Bellair Avenue and, at the margin, the City Sewerage Disposal Plant and pump station. Block numbers 89 to 116, 131, 232 to 236 and 270 to 275 are printed.
notes: South Broad Street is also lettered "(Zabriskie Av.)"; Brainard Place "(Woodside Pl.)"; Leonard Place "(Fairview Pl.)"; Boyce Place "(Grandview Pl.)". Zabriskie is read from a full-resolution crop but the lettering is partly cut by the street line.
Ethelbert Av. and Ethelbert Place: OpenStreetMap has Ethelbert Place; Lenox and Richmond are Lenox Avenue and Richmond Avenue.
Beyond the Ridgewood and Glen Rock village limits the sheet reads 'See Map of Glen Rock' and is blank.
The lettering Christopher Pl. and Randolph Pl. was read from the overview.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Erie main line down the middle; S. Broad (Zabriskie Av), Essex, Le Roy Pl, Brainard Pl (Woodside Pl), Woodside Av, Leonard Pl, Boyce Pl, Highwood Av, Edwards, Doremus, Ethelbert, Lenox, Richmond, Christopher, Randolph, Bellair, Pomander Walk; gas plant, sewage plant; Glen Rock blank at lower right.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the east side of Ridgewood's business centre and the blocks to the southeast, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Franklin Avenue runs along the top and East Ridgewood Avenue and Dayton Street cross the middle; North and South Walnut Street, Beech, Cottage Place and North and South Maple Avenue run across them. At the left Van Neste Square borders City Park, an open block. Commercial and institutional buildings stand mostly along East Ridgewood Avenue and Maple Avenue: the New Jersey Bell Telephone Co. building, a fire-proof structure of 1929, a Public Service building near Beech Street, auto sales and service buildings, a garage, a filling station, a mortuary, and the Beech Street School. Emmanuel Baptist Church with its Sunday school, the M.E. Church and a Reformed Church are also shown, and a public school stands on Union Street. Between the business streets and Spring Avenue the blocks hold detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings on Walton Street, Union Street and Prospect Street, which run diagonally to the southeast. In the lower left corner Woodside Avenue, Passaic Street and Boyce Place (Grandview Place) lead into the district drawn on sheet 19, and a hall stands on Maple Avenue. The right edge continues onto sheet 21 along Hope Street, and block numbers 196 to 205, 236 to 244 and 276 are printed. A compass rose sits at the upper left.
notes: Several streets carry bracketed old prefixes, for example "(W.) Franklin Av.", "(N.) Walnut" and "E.(W.) Ridgewood Av.".
Beech is drawn where OpenStreetMap places Cottage Place.
Boyce Pl. is also lettered "(Grandview Pl.)".
Names were read from the overview and checked against crops only where the lettering was small.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. East side of the business centre: Franklin Av to Spring Av, Oak, Walnut, Beech, Cottage Pl, Van Neste Sq, Maple, Dayton, Walton, Union, Hudson, Passaic, Prospect, Woodside; City Park.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the eastern edge of Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet is cut diagonally by Hohokus Brook, which winds from the top centre to the bottom edge, and by the right of way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co., an electric line, which runs beside it and is crossed by steel bridges at East Ridgewood Avenue and Spring Avenue. Between Franklin Avenue and East Ridgewood Avenue, North Irving Street and Marshall Avenue run to the northwest, and long narrow lots in blocks 200 and 202 hold small detached dwellings. South of East Ridgewood Avenue the district west of the brook is a regular grid of Hope Street, Liberty Street, South Irving Street and Southern Parkway crossed by Addison Place and Evergreen Place, filled with one- and two-storey frame dwellings; block 208 between East Ridgewood Avenue and Addison Place is open. East of the brook, Ridgewood High School, with a chapel, and a gymnasium stand on a large tract between Hermance Road and Brookside Avenue, and a Ridgewood High School athletic field is lettered beside the brook. Beverly Road runs along the top of the eastern part, with a row of detached houses, and Brookside Avenue, Hanks Avenue and Gordon Road open out the blocks below East Ridgewood Avenue, which are largely vacant apart from scattered dwellings. A compass rose stands at the top. Block numbers 199 to 214 and 247 to 254 are printed; the adjoining sheets named at the margins are 13, 14, 20, 22 and 25.
notes: Southern Parkway is also lettered "(Park Pl.)".
Hermance Rd. is Heermance Place in OpenStreetMap. Marshall Avenue is Marshall Street in OpenStreetMap, whose line lies 20 to 40 m from the drawn street and was left out of the fit.
North Irving and South Irving are lettered N. Irving and S. Irving.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. right of way (Elec.) crosses the sheet beside Hohokus Brook.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. (E.) Franklin, N./S. Irving, E. Ridgewood, Hope, Liberty, Southern Parkway, Addison, Evergreen, Brookside, Hermance Rd, Beverly, Marshall Av; Hohokus Brook, Ridgewood High School athletic field. Marshall left out (OSM 20-40 m off).

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers an eastern residential district of Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. East Ridgewood Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from west to east, and Van Dien Avenue (North and South) runs north-south through the left centre, with Beverly Road and Wyndemere Avenue along the top and (East) Spring Avenue along the bottom. The upper centre is largely open ground in blocks 215 and 219, apart from the glasshouses and sheds of F. C. Schweinfurth Inc., Florist, whose greenhouses are lettered 'Green Hos.' and stand in long rows. To the right, John Street and North Pleasant Avenue bound a block of narrow lots (block 223) with small dwellings, and the right edge is South Pleasant Avenue. South of East Ridgewood Avenue are the First Presbyterian Church and its Sunday school on South Van Dien Avenue, Fire Department Engine Company No. 2, and the Kenilworth School on Kenilworth Road. Circle Avenue curves through the lower centre between Spring Avenue and East Ridgewood Avenue, and a playground is lettered on the right. West of Van Dien Avenue the blocks along Brookside Avenue, Hanks Avenue and Gordon Road (Bergen Avenue) hold detached frame dwellings. Houses on the sheet are almost all one or two storeys with frame garages. A compass rose appears at the upper left, and a piece of Ridgewood High School shows at the left edge. Block numbers 214 to 223, 256 to 264 are printed, and the neighbouring sheets named at the margins are 14, 15, 21, 23, 25 and 26.
notes: Gordon Rd. is also lettered "(Bergen Av.)" and Kenilworth Rd. "(Pl.)".
The playground lettered on the right lies in block 264, east of Kenilworth Road.
John Street / Wyndemere Avenue was not detected.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Wyndemere, Beverly, Van Dien, E. Ridgewood, John, N./S. Pleasant, Frederick, Brookside, Hanks, Gordon Rd (Bergen Av), Circle, Kenilworth, (E.) Spring; Schweinfurth florist greenhouses.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the eastern edge of Ridgewood along East Ridgewood Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. At the left, North and South Pleasant Avenue run the height of the sheet, and Walthery Avenue runs parallel a little to the east, from Wyndemere Avenue at the top to East Ridgewood Avenue. Between them and below Wyndemere Avenue the blocks (227 to 230) are subdivided into narrow lots with detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings; Frederick Street crosses them. Immediately east of Walthery Avenue a strip of lots with dwellings backs onto a large open tract, blocks 228 and 231, that is almost entirely vacant. In it stand an ice house and a pond with a rectangular outline and shaded margin. South of East Ridgewood Avenue and east of South Pleasant Avenue the sheet holds a large cemetery (block 266) with a few dwellings at its upper left, and below it small houses on lots along Pleasant Avenue and (East) Spring Avenue. East Side Avenue and Carlock Avenue run south from East Ridgewood Avenue, where a short row of commercial buildings includes a garage, a filling station and an auto repair building. At the right edge the Ridgewood Midland Park Washing Co. Inc., a steam laundry, stands beside a stream that crosses the lower right and the top right corner. Large blocks 267 and 268 below East Ridgewood Avenue are mostly unbuilt. A compass rose is at the right, and neighbouring sheets 15, 22 and 26 are named at the margins.
notes: Frederick is lettered "Frederick (Fredrick)".
East Side Av. is Somerville Road in OpenStreetMap; Carlock Av. is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The laundry at the right edge is lettered "Ridgewood Midland Park Washing Co. Inc. (Laundry)".
Detection found no control east of East Side Avenue (9 points, all on the western half); the eastern part of the sheet rests on the fit's extrapolation.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. Wyndemere, Walthery, Frederick, N./S. Pleasant, E. Ridgewood, East Side Av (now Somerville Road), Carlock Av, (E.) Spring; pond, Ridgewood Midland Park Washing Co. laundry. Control only in the western half.

sheet-24-1.description: The main part of sheet 24 covers the southern edge of Ridgewood village against the Glen Rock boundary, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from Spring Avenue (labelled '(W.) Spring Av.' and '(E.) Spring Av.') at the top, where Union Street and South Maple Avenue meet it, south to the dash-dot village limits, beyond which the sheet is blank and marked 'See Map of Glen Rock'. Hope Street forms the east edge. Prospect Street runs diagonally across the sheet from Spring Avenue, crossing South Maple Avenue at a fire alarm box and continuing southeast past Cedar Avenue and Dunbar Avenue. West of South Maple Avenue the blocks are laid out along Woodside Avenue, Boyce Place (Grandview Place), Watlington Place, Carlisle Terrace (High), Ivy Place, Linden, High and Highwood Avenue; east of it Stilwell Place and Stilwell Road run down to the village limits, with Park Avenue and Norwood Avenue just beyond. The district is almost entirely detached dwellings of one to three storeys, many large and some of tile or stone, with auto garages; a few lots near Spring Avenue are marked 'From Plans'. There are stores of tile construction and a cinder-block dwelling on South Maple Avenue near Spring Avenue, and a lumber shed off Stilwell Place. A large vacant tract east of South Maple Avenue is crossed by an unopened, unnamed street. The lower left corner is cut off by a heavy line enclosing a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Spring Avenue is labelled "(W.) Spring Av." west and "(E.) Spring Av." east of South Maple Avenue.
Carlisle Terrace is labelled with the name High in brackets; a separate street labelled High meets Highwood Avenue further southwest (High Street in OpenStreetMap).
Boyce Place is labelled with the earlier name Grandview Place in brackets.
Dunbar Avenue and Watlington Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Prospect, Hope, Union and Linden are Prospect Street, Hope Street, Union Street and Linden Street in OpenStreetMap.
South of the Ridgewood and Glen Rock village limits the sheet is blank: 'See Map of Glen Rock'.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Spring Av, Union, S. Maple Av, Prospect, Hope, Cedar Av, Dunbar Av, Woodside Av, Boyce Pl (Grandview Pl), Watlington Pl, Carlisle Ter (High), Ivy Pl, Linden, High, Highwood Av, Stilwell Pl and Rd; south of the village limits 'See Map of Glen Rock'. Part 2 (lower-left inset behind a heavy line): Orchard Pl, Demarest, Doremus Av, Ackerman Av, Erie main line; helmert-like 3-point fit.

sheet-24-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 24 is an inset in the lower left corner, enclosed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing toward the upper left. It shows a small area on the southwest edge of Ridgewood, around Orchard Place between Demarest and Doremus Avenue, with Ackerman Avenue running diagonally along its eastern side beside the Erie Railroad main line, whose tracks are drawn in the lower right corner of the inset. The dash-dot Ridgewood and Glen Rock village limits cross the lower part of the inset, and the ground beyond is blank and marked 'See Map of Glen Rock'. The blocks hold a few one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages along Orchard Place and Doremus Avenue, and a store or similar building with a blue (stone) and yellow (frame) section north of Orchard Place. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches run in Doremus and Ackerman Avenues. The inset sits on the ground next to sheet 19, whose number is printed at its top edge.
notes: Inset drawn separately from the main map of sheet 24; it adjoins sheet 19.
Demarest is Demarest Street in OpenStreetMap.
OpenStreetMap has two Ackerman Avenue / Doremus Avenue nodes about 78 m apart; the southern one (40.97335) was used.
E. R. R. (Main Line) tracks are drawn in the lower right corner.

Map, 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Spring Av, Union, S. Maple Av, Prospect, Hope, Cedar Av, Dunbar Av, Woodside Av, Boyce Pl (Grandview Pl), Watlington Pl, Carlisle Ter (High), Ivy Pl, Linden, High, Highwood Av, Stilwell Pl and Rd; south of the village limits 'See Map of Glen Rock'. Part 2 (lower-left inset behind a heavy line): Orchard Pl, Demarest, Doremus Av, Ackerman Av, Erie main line; helmert-like 3-point fit.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers the southeastern edge of Ridgewood next to the Glen Rock boundary, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. (East) Spring Avenue runs along the top, and South Irving Street runs south from it as the sheet's main street, curving at the top and crossing Hawthorne Place, Cedar Avenue, Dunbar Avenue and Arden Court. The area is thinly built: detached one- and two-storey dwellings stand along South Irving Street and its side streets, and several larger parcels (blocks 250, 252, 283 and 253) are open or hold only a few houses. In the upper left a strip of narrow lots with small garages stands along Cedar Avenue, and two unopened streets are lettered 'Not Named' and 'Not Opened'. Hohokus Brook winds down the right centre of the sheet, beside the abandoned right of way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric), and a steel bridge carries Spring Avenue over it. Where Grove street crosses the brook and the line across the lower part marks the Ridgewood and Glen Rock village limits, the area beyond is lettered 'See Map of Glen Rock' and left blank, as is the strip along Prospect Street at the lower left. A fire-proof transformer building stands near the brook at the village line. At the right edge Brookside Avenue and block numbers 255, 259, 286 and 292 mark the adjoining ground of sheets 22 and 26. A compass rose sits in the brook. Block numbers 250 to 255, 283 to 286 and 292 are printed.
notes: Hawthorne Pl. is also lettered "(Av.)" and Arden Ct. "(Irving Pl.)".
Dunbar Avenue is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Sheet 24 and 'See Map of Glen Rock' are noted beyond the village limits, which are blank.
Only seven points were found, mostly along South Irving Street, and the leave-one-out error is larger than on other sheets.

Map, 100 ft. Single part. (E.) Spring, Hope, S. Irving, Hawthorne Pl (Av), Cedar, Dunbar, Arden Ct (Irving Pl), Brookside, Prospect, Glendale Rd, Grove; Hohokus Brook; Glen Rock blank at bottom. Few points (7).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers the southeastern corner of Ridgewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. (East) Spring Avenue runs along the top and Grove street along the lower part; South Van Dien Avenue bounds the left side, Kenilworth Road and Stevens Avenue run through the middle, and South Pleasant Avenue runs along the right. Circle Avenue, Lotus Road and Laurel Road complete a regular grid of blocks (261 to 265, 287 to 290 and 628) that are filled with detached one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, mostly in the upper two thirds of the sheet. The lower blocks (289, 291, 292, 293 and 629) are larger and almost empty, with a few scattered houses. At the left edge, west of South Van Dien Avenue, Peter L. Zabriskie's planning mill and lumber yard occupies several sheds and lumber piles. A few small buildings, two of them tinted pink, stand beside Grove street at the left. Hens' houses and small outbuildings are lettered in the upper blocks. The right margin shows a few buildings along South Pleasant Avenue and Grove street. A compass rose stands on the right. Neighbouring sheets 22, 23 and 25 are named at the margins.
notes: Kenilworth Rd. is also lettered "(Pl.)" and Stevens Av. "(Wykagyl Pl.)".
Grove street is drawn narrower (about 35 ft between edges) than its modern right-of-way (about 55 ft), so its junctions carry larger residuals.
Peter L. Zabriskie's planning mill stands at the left edge.
Map, 100 ft. Single part. (E.) Spring, S. Van Dien, Circle, Kenilworth Rd (Pl), Lotus, Laurel, Stevens Av (Wykagyl Pl), S. Pleasant, Grove; Zabriskie planing mill.
